content: MK's survey of the Munshaʾāt-i Ṣāʾin-i Turka finds frequent dealings with Timurid amirs and a particularly close relationship with Bāysunghur b. Shāhrukh, and friendly relations with prominent Iranian Sufis: Shāh Niʿmat Allāh Valī, Qāsim-i Anvār, Aḥmad Samarqandī, Ḥasan ʿAṭṭār and Sayyid Muḥammad b. Shaykh Kajujī. He says this corroborates what the apologies say of his dealings with Sufi shaykhs (mainly in an admonitory role) and counterbalances his criticism of organized Sufism elsewhere.
